That's real pain, not just discomfort you can train through, so here's my honest answer: this needs a doctor or physical therapist to look at before we build anything around your squat. Sharp pain at the bottom of a lift, plus soreness that lingers into the next day, isn't something I should diagnose or guess at over text - and I'd rather you get it checked than have me program around something neither of us can see.

I'm not going to write you a squat progression today. Once you've been seen and have some idea what's going on - whether that's "you're fine, here's what to watch for" or "avoid this position for now" - bring that back to me and I'll build the program around it, including your other lifts.

In the meantime, I'm still your coach for everything else. If you want to talk about bench or deadlift, or just want to know what a PT visit for this usually looks like so it feels less like a mystery, I'm here for that. And for what it's worth - stopping the session when it grabbed you was the right call, not something to be embarrassed about.

reply:
Got it - that's a real answer, and it's useful to know.

That connects to something worth naming once: at 18 drinks a week, the concrete cost isn't really "hurts your squat number" - the actual studies show a single night out doesn't wreck next-day force output much. It's the sleep and the Saturday-morning state that's doing the damage here, and that's exactly what you just described.

So: if Friday night happens the way it usually does, what's the smallest thing you'd actually do instead of skipping the session entirely? Doesn't have to be heroic - "still show up and just do the warm-up sets" counts as a plan. What would you commit to on the worst version of that Saturday?

reply:
Good to meet you. Before we get into programming, I want to flag something from your intake: you noted sharp lower back pain when deadlifting, starting about two weeks ago, and that you haven't had it looked at yet.

I'm not going to write you a program around that - not a modified one, not a "everything except deadlift" one, nothing. That's not me being overly cautious for no reason: I can't tell what's actually affected just because it showed up during a deadlift. That's a question for someone who can examine you, not something either of us can guess our way past. I'd rather lose a week to an appointment than have you load a spine that needs a look first.

Here's what I'd suggest: get in front of a doctor or physical therapist. When you go, it'll help them if you can describe - when exactly it started, what specifically brings it on (first rep? last rep? bending after?), whether it stays local or radiates anywhere (butt, leg, foot), and what makes it feel better or worse day to day. If you want, there's a page - coachdiaz.app/about - written specifically for a clinician, explaining what this app is and how they can set training restrictions that I'll build around. No account needed, you can just show it to them.

Once you're cleared - however they clear you, fully or with limits - I'll build the program around whatever they say, starting from the lifts and experience you've already given me. I'm not going anywhere in the meantime. Happy to talk through bracing, how progression works, what a first weeks of training generally looks like, or answer anything else on your mind while you get that sorted.
